commitments.text: Condition 1(1) must be interpreted so that the contents of the later dated document will vary, repeal, rescind or supersede, as the case may be, the contents of earlier dated documents listed in Schedule A. 1(3) Where, in the reasonable opinion of the Executive Director, there is a conflict or inconsistency between any of the documents listed in Schedule A to this Certificate and the Conditions which follow, these Conditions must take precedence over and supersede the contents of the documents listed in Schedule A. 1(4) CPC must advise the Executive Director of the actual nameplate capacity of the Powerplant once it has been specified by the construction contractor and if the nameplate capacity is not less than 130 MW and not greater than 170 MW there will not, in the absence of other change, be considered to have been a change in the design, location, construction or operation of the Project.

Notwithstanding Condition 1(1), but subject to Condition 1(4), if, prior to operation of the Project, CPC proposes a change to the design, location, construction or operation of the Project as described in Schedule A that is likely to have significant adverse effects not reviewed and addressed to the satisfaction of the Project Committee, CPC must: (a) provide notice of the proposed change to the Executive Director; and (b) where the Executive Director, in consultation with the appropriate provincial authorities, reasonably considers that the proposed change is likely to have significant adverse effects not reviewed and addressed to the satisfaction of the Project Committee, provide the Executive Director with plans, analyses, records and other information necessary for an effective assessment by the Executive Director of the proposed change.
CPC must, in the reasonable opinion of the Minister, have substantially started construction of the Powerplant within five years of the date of issuance of this Certificate.

This Certificate does not constitute a permit, licence, approval or any other authority required under any other enactment. CPC must to the reasonable satisfaction of the Minister comply with all orders, directions and conditions, and obtain and must comply with all applicable tenures, licences, regulations, approvals, standards and permits, which may include or result from all enactments including the Agricultural Land Commission Act, Fish Protection Act, Forest Practices Code of B.C. Act, Heritage Conservation Act, Pesticide Control Act, Transport of Dangerous Goods Act, Waste Management Act and Water Act.
The Project must not be operated for daily load flow shaping without the prior written approval of the Comptroller of Water Rights ("CWR").

CPC must enter into an agreement with the British Columbia Hydro and Power Authority ("BC Hydro") that will provide details to the CWR of the operation of the Project with the storage releases from the Arrow Reservoir, and that operating agreement must provide to the reasonable satisfaction of the CWR that: (a) storage operations required by the Columbia River Treaty will be satisfied, including operational arrangements for the Project to ensure that all existing requirements for minimum flows and ramping rates will be implemented and that the Keenleyside Dam will continue to be operated such that water not discharged through the Powerplant will continue to be discharged preferentially through the north low level outlets rather than the spillway and the south low level outlets, or in such other manner as is determined to minimize the level of Total Dissolved Gasses in the Columbia River downstream; (b) current opportunities to implement beneficial operations for fish and other environmental objectives will not be diminished; and (c) operation of Arrow Reservoir will not be materially altered due to Project construction.

CPC must to the reasonable satisfaction of the District Highways Manager prior to commencement of the relocation of Broadwater Road: (a) submit plans for the relocation of the Broadwater Road for written approval; (b) commit to pay all construction costs for the relocation of the Broadwater Road; (c) undertake the Broadwater Road relocation in such a way as to avoid disrupting traffic during July and August; and (d) notify District Parks Manager, Ministry of Environment, Lands and Parks, the Director for Area I of the Regional District of Central Kootenay and residents in the Robson area prior to start of road construction to ensure that road access to the Arrow Reservoir is not unduly disrupted due to construction activities.

CPC must to the reasonable satisfaction of the District Highways Manager: (a) conduct, in co-operation with the District Highways Manager, a pre-construction survey of the road structure and pavement condition of Robson Road and Broadwater Road prior to the start of Powerplant construction, and a post-construction survey upon completion of Powerplant construction; (b) based on these surveys, identify the adverse effects of the Powerplant construction on Robson Road and Broadwater Road; and (c) propose mitigation and compensation measures for review and written approval by the District Highways Manager, and upon such approval implement these measures.

CPC must to the reasonable satisfaction of the District Highways Manager, develop a Traffic Management Plan in accordance with the Terms of Reference, Traffic Management Plan, Project Report, Volume 1, Appendix C, Tab 3, and in so doing, must: (a) make the Traffic Management Plan available for comment to the District Highways Manager, the Regional Manager, Fish Wildlife and Habitat, Ministry of Environment, Lands and Parks, the City of Castlegar, the Regional Director for Area I, District of Central Kootenay and local residents; (b) submit the Traffic Management Plan to District Highways Manager and the City of Castlegar for their review and written approval prior to start of Powerplant construction; and (c) upon such approval implement the approved Traffic Management Plan.

CPC must to the reasonable satisfaction of the District Highways Manager, develop a Public Safety Management Plan in accordance with the Terms of Reference, Public Safety Management Plan, Project Report, Volume 1, Appendix C, Tab 4, and in so doing, must: (a) make the Public Safety Management Plan available for comment to the District Highways Manager, the City of Castlegar, the Regional District of Central Kootenay and local residents; (b) submit the Public Safety Management Plan to MOTH for review and written approval prior to start of Powerplant construction; and (c) upon such approval, implement the approved Public Safety Management Plan.

CPC must: (a) prepare, and make available for comment to the Regional Manager, Fish, Wildlife and Habitat, and the Regional Manager, Environmental Protection, Ministry of Environment, Lands and Parks, Department of Fisheries and Oceans ("DFO") and Columbia Basin First Nations, an Environmental Management Plan for the Powerplant in accordance with the Terms of Reference, Environmental Management Plan Outline, contained in Volume 1, Appendix C, Tab 1 of Project Report; (b) submit the Environmental Management Plan to the CWR for review and written approval prior to start of Powerplant construction; and (c) upon such approval, implement the approved Environmental Management Plan.

Prior to start of Powerplant construction, CPC must retain the services of a qualified Environmental Monitor, to ensure to the reasonable satisfaction of the CWR, compliance with all aspects of the Environmental Management Plan. The Environmental Monitor must report to the Powerplant construction manager, and must have the authority as prescribed in the terms of reference to cease construction activities of the Powerplant if not in compliance with the Environmental Management Plan.

CPC must to the reasonable satisfaction of the CWR: (a) implement the KPP150 Temperature Management Approach, submitted January 26, 1998, as described in Tab 7, Supplemental Volume, Project Report; (b) commence temperature monitoring in the first thermally stratified season following issuance of this Certificate for the Project; and (c) develop and implement temperature mitigation measures, if determined to be necessary by the CWR in accordance with KPP150 Temperature Management Approach and such measures must be circulated for comment to the Regional Manager, Environmental Protection, DFO and Columbia Basin First Nations.

CPC must to the reasonable satisfaction of the CWR: (a) design the tailrace orientation from the Project at a 135 degree angle from true North to mitigate the adverse effects of powerplant discharges on eddy habitats.

CPC must to the reasonable satisfaction of the CWR: (b) monitor the physical and biological effects of the Project on eddy habitats in accordance with the KPP150 Powerplant Project Downstream Flow Patterns Proposed Monitoring of Eddy Habitats, submitted February 16, 1998; and (c) develop mitigation measures for adverse effects on eddy habitats if determined to be necessary by the CWR, and such measures must be circulated for comment to the Regional Manager, Fish, Wildlife and Habitat, DFO and Columbia Basin First Nations.

CPC must: (a) prepare and circulate for comment to DFO and Columbia Basin First Nations, and submit prior to start of Powerplant construction, a detailed fish habitat mitigation plan in accordance with the conceptual Fish Habitat Mitigation Plan, submitted December 19, 1997, for habitat lost to spoil placement in the Arrow Reservoir drawdown area; (b) submit the detailed fish habitat mitigation plan for review and written approval by the Regional Manager, Fish, Wildlife and Habitat; and (c) upon such approval implement the approved plan.

CPC must submit a spill contingency plan to the Regional Manager, Environmental Protection, for review and written approval, such approval not to be unreasonably withheld or delayed, prior to start of Powerplant construction, and adhere to the approved spill contingency plan.

CPC must: (a) prepare, and circulate for comment to the Regional Manager, Fish, Wildlife and Habitat, DFO, Canadian Wildlife Service, Columbia Basin First Nations and Regional District of Central Kootenay, a final Development and Reclamation Plan; (b) submit the final Development and Reclamation Plan for review and written approval by the CWR, prior to start of Powerplant construction; and (c) upon such approval implement the approved plan.

CPC must: (a) provide compensation for the Project's effects on fish entrainment and habitat loss, in accordance with the Compensation Plan in the Project Report, Volume 1, Section 7.2.2 - Operations Compensation; and (b) monitor the effects of the Compensation Plan in accordance with Fish Entrainment Compensation Monitoring Plan described in Project Report, Volume 1, Appendix C, Tab 7.

CPC must, commencing April 1st of the year following the start of Powerplant construction, and thereafter, for so long as fish may be entrained by the Project, pay in accordance with the Compensation Plan an annual contribution of $175,000 to be adjusted for inflation on April 1st of each subsequent year by the Vancouver Consumer Price Index as published by Statistics Canada: (a) to the Columbia Basin Fish and Wildlife Compensation Program ("CBFWCP") for implementing and monitoring a partnered Upper and Lower Arrow Reservoir fertilization program.

CPC must submit a Socio-Economic Monitoring Program in accordance with the Terms of Reference, Socio-Economic Monitoring Program, KPP150 Consolidated Project Report, Volume 1, Appendix C, Tab 5, for review and written approval by the City of Castlegar, the Regional District of Central Kootenay, and the Regional District of Kootenay Boundary prior to start of Powerplant construction, and upon such approval must implement the approved Socio-Economic Monitoring Program.

CPC must establish prior to start of Powerplant construction, a Community Impact Management Committee consisting of one or more representatives from CPC, the City of Castlegar, the Regional District of Central Kootenay, the Regional District of Kootenay Boundary and any other agencies as agreed by the foregoing Committee representatives, to resolve any Project construction issues affecting community services and infrastructure.

CPC must retain a Socio-Economic Monitor to oversee the Socio-Economic Monitoring Program, monitor Project-related socio-economic effects and liaise with community representatives and the Community Impact Management Committee.

CPC must provide, prior to start of Powerplant construction, $75,000 in funding to the Castlegar and District Recreation Commission for facilities at Pass Creek Regional Park to compensate for increased demands on local parks and the loss of Driftwood Beach due to the Project, and $75,000 to the Minister of Finance and Corporate Relations for deposit to a dedicated account for Syringa Creek Provincial Park, as compensation for all impacts on Syringa Creek Provincial Park caused by the Project.

CPC must to the reasonable satisfaction of the Responsible Minister, negotiate in good faith with Columbia Basin First Nations to achieve and implement First Nations employment agreements consistent with the terms of the agreement between the Columbia Hydro Constructors and the Allied Hydro Council, and achieve and implement First Nations economic development programs.

CPC must to the reasonable satisfaction of the CWR: (a) develop and identify the final alignment of the Transmission Line, within the Transmission Line corridor identified in the Supplemental Volume, Project Report, Tab 10, prior to Transmission Line clearing and after providing reasonable opportunity for input from landowners in the immediate vicinity of the proposed Transmission Line, the Regional Manager, Fish, Wildlife and Habitat, the Ministry of Small Business, Tourism and Culture, the Ministry of Forests, DFO, Canadian Wildlife Service, Agricultural Land Commission, Columbia Basin First Nations, Regional District of Central Kootenay and Regional District of Kootenay Boundary; and (b) subject to Condition 28, design, construct and operate the Transmission Line in accordance with the commitments, responsibilities and assurances for the Transmission Line noted in the Supplemental Volume, Project Report, Tab 11, Table 3.

CPC must: (a) prepare an Environmental Management Plan for the Transmission Line in accordance with the Terms of Reference, Preparation of an Environmental Management Plan for the Keenleyside Project 230 kV Transmission Line, after providing reasonable opportunity for input from DFO, Canadian Wildlife Service, Regional Manager, Fish, Wildlife and Habitat, Regional Manager, Lands and Water, Ministry of Environment, Lands and Parks, Regional District of Central Kootenay, Regional District of Kootenay Boundary and Columbia Basin First Nations; (b) submit the Environmental Management Plan for review and written approval by the CWR prior to the start of Transmission Line clearing; and (c) upon such approval implement the approved plan.

CPC must to the reasonable satisfaction of the Manager, Planning and Assessment, Archaeology Branch, Ministry of Small Business, Tourism and Culture: (a) undertake and submit a detailed archaeological impact assessment of the proposed Transmission Line final alignment prepared by a qualified archaeologist at least one year prior to clearing or ground disturbance activities; (b) if archaeological resources are identified in locations along the proposed Transmission Line final alignment as a result of the detailed impact assessment, after allowing reasonable opportunity for input by Columbia Basin First Nations, implement all necessary management measures in accordance with the Heritage Conservation Act and the BC Archaeological Impact Assessment Guidelines; and (c) implement all necessary emergency management measures in accordance with the Heritage Conservation Act and the BC Archaeological Impact Assessment Guidelines, if any archaeological resources subject to the Heritage Conservation Act are identified during ground clearing or construction activities and advise Columbia Basin First Nations.

CPC must to the reasonable satisfaction of the CWR, as part of detailed alignment, design and mitigation planning for the Transmission Line: (a) undertake a detailed assessment of potential Transmission Line impacts on First Nations traditional uses; (b) identify mitigation and/or compensation measures for Columbia Basin First Nations to prevent or reduce any effects on traditional use activities to an acceptable level; and (c) submit the traditional use assessment and proposed mitigation and compensation measures to the CWR for review and approval, prior to a decision on the final alignment of the Transmission Line.

2(2)(a) For the purposes of this Certificate, the term "prior to start of Powerplant construction" and similar references do not prevent the levelling of Area 2 with overburden from Area 3 as shown on the Drawings LY-1 to LY-5 dated February 12, 1999 for the setting up of temporary office and yard facilities, subject to CPC obtaining all necessary provincial, municipal and regional approvals. 2(2)(b) No work or clearing in Area 2 and Area 3 may take place within 15 metres of the top of the bank of the Columbia River, except as approved in writing by the Regional Manager, Environmental Protection, and no Powerplant construction can proceed except in accordance with the Conditions of this Certificate.

2(2)(c) CPC shall ensure that the Environmental Monitor is monitoring Areas 2 and 3 whenever activities are taking place, in accordance with the latest draft of the Environmental Management Plan submitted to the Comptroller of Water Rights ("CWR").

8(1) CPC must to the reasonable satisfaction of the CWR: i. prior to start of Powerplant construction, enter into an agreement with the British Columbia Hydro and Power Authority for the diversion and use of water from the Arrow Reservoir, and the agreement must be submitted to the CWR; and ii. prior to start of Powerplant operation, demonstrate that the agreement provides details of how: a. storage operations required by the Columbia River Treaty will be satisfied, including operational arrangements for the Project to ensure that all existing requirements for minimum flows and ramping rates will be implemented and that the Keenleyside Dam will continue to be operated such that water not discharged through the Powerplant will continue to be discharged preferentially throughout the north low level outlets rather than the spillway and the south low level outlets, or in such other manner as is determined to minimize the level of Total Dissolved Gasses in the Columbia River downstream; and b. current opportunities to implement beneficial operations for fish and other environmental objectives will not be diminished. 8(2) CPC must ensure that the agreement specifies that the operation of Arrow Reservoir will not be materially altered due to Project construction.

Conduct, in co-operation with the District Highways Manager, an initial survey of the road structure and pavement condition of Robson Road and Broadwater Road prior to the start of Powerplant construction (or as soon thereafter as frost is no longer present in the road structure), and a post construction survey upon completion of Powerplant construction.

The use of Ammonium Nitrate Fuel Oil (ANFO) as an explosive will be prohibited and only low nitrate explosives will be permitted, provided however ANFO may be used under the following conditions: i. in dry holes above the water table; ii. in accordance with DFO Guidelines for use of explosives in Canadian fisheries waters; iii. if appropriate precautions are taken to ensure complete detonation of the ammonium nitrate; iv. if any excavated rock contaminated with unexploded ammonium nitrate is disposed of only in a designated area where it cannot contaminate ground water or enter watercourses; v. if effluent from rock excavations is monitored for nitrogen compounds and treated or disposed of in accordance with the approved Environmental Management Plan.
Except for dredging done within the area protected by a silt curtain, dredging will be done with a sealed clamshell bucket.

The use of chemicals for dust suppression on roads will be prohibited except that calcium chloride may be used as a dust suppressant in Area 2 provided that it is used in accordance with the Ministry of Transportation and Highways Maintenance Standard for Dust Control and the Department of Fisheries and Oceans conditions contained in their letter 5300-10-002 dated May 11, 1999.
